# openprovider_domain_renewal (Resource)

Renews a domain for a period of years, and charges the account for it. The renewal occurs when Terraform creates or replaces the resource; a change of an attribute that the configuration sets replaces the resource, so use `triggers` to renew again. The apply fails, and the provider sends no renewal, when the account has no such domain, when the domain is not active, or when OpenProvider does not allow a renewal of the domain now (see `can_renew` of the `openprovider_domains` data source). The deletion of the resource does not change the domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openprovider_domains" "example" {
  full_name = "example.com"
}

# Renew example.com for two years, once. The account is charged.
resource "openprovider_domain_renewal" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
  period = 2

  # Change a value to renew again.
  triggers = {
    renewal = "2027"
  }
}

output "can_renew" {
  value = data.openprovider_domains.example.domains[0].can_renew
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain name (e.g., example.com).

### Optional

- `period` (Number) The period of the renewal in years, from 1 to 10. Defaults to 1. The registry limits the total registration period of the domain.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values. A change of a value renews the domain again.

### Read-Only

- `expiration_date` (String) When the registration expires, as read after the renewal. The registry can take a while to move it.
- `id` (String) The domain name.
- `status` (String) The status that OpenProvider answered the renewal with.
